title: feat(worktree-guard): add an opt-in base-branch refusal mode
body:
<!-- idd-skill-authoring-publication: target=target-912dc6402a2a0a4a; anchor=kurone-kito/idd-skill#2795; set=set-01ab237a36117ba2; session=claude-sonnet5-15b9d1f4; token=pub-49428997b293f039 -->

## Background

The shipped `worktreeGuard` hook (`.githooks/_idd-worktree-guard.sh`,
`idd-skill#2233`'s own fix) refuses a commit/push made from the primary
worktree only when `HEAD` matches a configured `branchPatterns` glob
(default `issue/* roadmap-audit/*`). Confirmed by reading the script
directly: its `case "$branch" in $pattern)` loop has no special case for
the configured default/base branch itself, so a delegated worker that
skips B1 entirely and commits directly on the base branch (e.g. `main`)
in the primary worktree is never refused -- `branch` evaluates to the
literal base-branch name, which matches neither default pattern.

The B1 self-check (`idd-skill#2233`'s other shipped mitigation) is blind
here from a different angle: it is a checkpoint written *inside* the B1
phase's own instructions, so it only helps an agent that actually reaches
and reads that phase file. An agent that skips straight from reading the
issue to writing implementation code never reads B1 at all in that
failure mode.

Field evidence: a delegated worker skipped both the claim step and the
entire B1 worktree-creation step, editing implementation source files
directly in the primary worktree while `HEAD` stayed on the base branch
the whole time. Caught via an unexpectedly non-empty `git status` before
any commit was attempted -- not a reproduced hook bypass on a real commit
-- but by direct inspection of the guard's own branch-matching logic, a
commit attempted from that exact state would not have been refused.

## Proposed change

Add an **opt-in**, off-by-default stricter mode to the guard: when enabled
via a new `worktreeGuard` config key (e.g. `refuseBaseBranchCommits:
true`, defaulting to `false` so existing adopters' behavior is unchanged),
also refuse a commit/push made from the primary worktree while `HEAD` is
on the repository's configured default branch. Keep this strictly opt-in
since a direct base-branch commit from the primary worktree is also a
legitimate, routine action for a human maintainer working outside an IDD
session -- the new key lets an adopter that wants the stricter guarantee
choose it explicitly, without changing the shipped default for anyone
else. Alongside the code change, document the hook's actual scope next to
its existing description (both in the hook's own header comment and in
`idd-work.instructions.md`'s B1), so the base-branch gap is a known,
documented limitation of the default mode rather than an implicit blind
spot.

## Acceptance criteria

- A new `worktreeGuard.refuseBaseBranchCommits` config key (or equivalent
  name) exists, defaulting to `false`/absent.
- When set to `true`, the hook refuses a commit/push from the primary
  worktree while `HEAD` is on the repository's configured default branch,
  with the same refusal message shape the existing pattern-match refusal
  uses.
- When unset or `false`, existing behavior is unchanged -- a base-branch
  commit from the primary worktree is still allowed by default.
- `tests/worktree-guard-hook.test.mts` covers both the new opt-in refusal
  case and the unchanged default-off case.
- The hook's own header comment and `idd-work.instructions.md`'s B1 state
  the guard's actual default scope (implementation-branch patterns only,
  not the base branch, unless the new opt-in is set).
- `node --experimental-strip-types --test tests/worktree-guard-hook.test.mts`
  passes.

## Candidate files

- `.githooks/_idd-worktree-guard.sh`
- `idd-template/.githooks/_idd-worktree-guard.sh`
- `tests/worktree-guard-hook.test.mts`
- `.github/instructions/idd-work.instructions.md`
- `idd-template/.github/instructions/idd-work.instructions.md`
- `schemas/policy.schema.json`
